Guava Atole

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Guava Atole is a warm, comforting traditional Mexican beverage made from masa (corn dough), sweetened with guava fruit. It is commonly enjoyed during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, a celebration honoring Mexico's patron saint where families gather to share traditional foods and drinks.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 1 cup (240 ml) guava juice or guava nectar
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine 2 cups of water and the cinnamon stick; bring to a simmer over medium heat.
  2. In a separate bowl, whisk the masa harina with the remaining 2 cups of water until smooth and no lumps remain.
  3. Slowly pour the masa mixture into the simmering water with cinnamon, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
  4. Add the guava juice, sugar, and salt to the saucepan, continuing to stir.
  5. Cook the mixture over low heat for about 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until it thickens to a creamy consistency.
  6. Remove from heat, discard the cinnamon stick, and stir in the vanilla extract.
  7. Serve hot in mugs, garnished with a cinnamon stick if desired.

Tips

  • Use fresh guava juice for a more authentic flavor or guava nectar for sweetness.
  • Adjust sugar to taste depending on the sweetness of your guava juice.
  • For a creamier texture, substitute half of the water with milk or evaporated milk.
